newly_blocked_claims.text: Sa ilalim ng Omnibus Rules, dapat igalang ng employer ang gustong araw ng pahinga ng empleyado kung ito ay base sa relihiyon, basta isusulat ito at ipapadala sa employer nang hindi bababa sa pitong (7) araw bago ang gustong petsa. Pero, kung ang pagpili ng empleyado ay tiyak na magdudulot ng malubhang pinsala o hadlang sa operasyon ng negosyo at wala nang ibang paraan para maayos ito, pwede ang employer na magtakda ng ibang araw ng pahinga para sa empleyado, pero hindi bababa sa dalawang (2) araw sa isang buwan.

Sa Art. 295 ng Labor Code, may exception sa regular‑employment rule: kung ang trabaho ay seasonal in nature at ang employment ay para lamang sa haba ng season, itinuturing itong seasonal exception. Ibig sabihin, ang kontrata ay valid lang habang tumatagal ang picking season at natatapos kapag natapos na ang season.

Sa ilalim ng Labor Advisory No. 06‑2020, kailangang ibigay ng employer ang Certificate of Employment (COE) sa loob ng tatlong (3) araw mula sa petsa ng kahilingan mo. Walang binanggit na “better policy” exception para sa COE, kaya kung sinabing aasikasuhin pa nila ito sa susunod na quarter, technically lumalabag ito sa itinakdang deadline.

When a seller or manufacturer gives an express warranty, the law requires the warranty to be written in clear, easily understood language and to include: the identity of the warrantor; the identity of the party to whom the warranty is extended; a description of the products or parts covered; a statement of what the warrantor will do if a defect, malfunction or non‑conformity occurs and who will pay for it; a description of what the consumer must do to claim the warranty; and the period within which the warrantor must act after notice of the problem. Any warranty that omits these elements is considered null and void.

Para mag-claim ng warranty, kailangan mo lang dalhin ang produkto kasama ang warranty card o resibo sa mismong nagbenta (immediate seller). Walang ibang dokumento na hihingin. Kung ang seller ay manufacturer showroom o distributor, dapat agad nilang ayusin o palitan ang item. Kapag ordinaryong retailer ang nagbenta, obligasyon niya na ipasa ang claim sa distributor nang walang bayad sa buyer; siya lang ang magdadala ng gastos kung hindi pa ito tinupad ng distributor o manufacturer.

Sa ilalim ng Art. 101 ng Consumer Act, kung ang net content ng produkto ay mas mababa kaysa sa nakasaad sa lalagyan, label o ad, ang supplier ay may pananagutan. Bilang consumer, pwede mong piliin ang isa sa mga sumusunod: (a) bayaran ang proportionate price ng natanggap mong tiles; (b) dagdagan ang timbang o sukat na kulang; (c) palitan ang pack ng kaparehong klase, tatak o modelo na walang kakulangan; o (d) ibalik agad ang buong bayad kasama ang monetary updating at posibleng damages. Ang supplier ay mananagot lalo na kung ang panukat na ginamit ay hindi naka‑calibrate ayon sa opisyal na pamantayan.

Sa ilalim ng Consumer Act, kung sinabing may sponsorship, approval, o affiliation ang isang produkto pero wala talaga, itinuturing itong deceptive practice. Ibig sabihin, ang seller na nag-claim na certified ang kettle pero hindi maipakita ang basehan ay maaaring lumabag sa batas dahil nagbigay ng false representation tungkol sa approval. Hindi kailangan patunayan agad na peke ang claim; ang mismong maling representasyon ay sapat na para ituring itong deceptive.

Before filing a case in court or with a government agency, the aggrieved party must first use the digital platform’s internal redress mechanism. That step is considered exhausted only when the platform has not resolved the complaint within seven calendar days from the date it was filed.

The law says the e‑retailer or online merchant is primarily liable for indemnifying the consumer for any breach arising from the internet transaction. The e‑marketplace or digital platform is only treated as liable in the same way as the merchant when a finding shows they are the same entity. Thus, liability rests with the merchant unless the platform is legally identified as the same party; the platform does not automatically bear responsibility for all purchase problems.

Para sa retail purchase, ang Art. 100 ay nagsasabing refund ay available lang kung may imperpeksiyon sa produkto at hindi ito na‑ayos sa loob ng 30 araw. Walang depekto, walang awtomatikong refund; ang retailer ay may subsidiaryong obligasyon sa warranty kung ang manufacturer o distributor ay hindi tumupad, pero hindi ito para sa simpleng pagbabago ng kulay na gusto mo.

Para sa 13th month pay, ang batas (PD 851) nagde‑define na ito ay katumbas ng isang‑twelfth (1/12) ng basic salary mo sa loob ng isang kalendaryong taon. Ang basic salary ay lahat ng sahod at benepisyo na binabayaran mo para sa trabaho, pero hindi kasama ang cost‑of‑living allowance, profit‑sharing, at iba pang allowance na hindi bahagi ng regular na sahod noong 1975. Sa Memorandum Order No. 28 (1986), sinabing lahat ng rank‑and‑file employees dapat makatanggap ng 13th month pay hindi lalampas ng Disyembre 24 bawat taon.

Sa ilalim ng Internet Transactions Act (RA 11967) at ng JAO 24‑03, kung may depekto, malfunction, o pagkawala ng produkto na hindi mo kasalanan, may karapatan kang humingi ng repair, replacement, o refund. Kapag pinili mo ang replacement o refund, ang online merchant ay may karapatang ibalik ang orihinal na item na ipinadala sa’yo nang walang bayad sa’yo, at dapat itong gawin sa loob ng makatwirang panahon maliban na lang kung may ibang napagkasunduan. Kung nabayaran na ang refund pero hindi mo maibalik ang item dahil sa iyong pagkakamali, kailangan mong ibalik ang perang natanggap, maaaring may proportionate reduction sa presyo.

For a covered employee, the employer must disclose, at the time of engagement, the specific standards that will determine whether the employee will qualify as regular. This requirement applies regardless of the nature of the work and must be communicated before the probationary period begins.

An express warranty must state the period within which the warrantor will act after a defect is reported. Any warranty that omits that period is void, because any stipulation contrary to the article is without legal effect.

The supplied source only covers consumer warranties, requiring the warranty to specify its enforceable period and rendering any omission void. No provision on probationary employment is present in these materials, so the employment question cannot be answered from the given sources.

Kung kulang ang dami ng tiles kumpara sa nakasaad sa label, may liability ang supplier para sa quantity imperfection (Art. 101). May karapatan ang consumer na pumili ng isa sa mga remedyo: bayaran ang proporsyonal na presyo, dagdagan ang nawawalang timbang o sukat, palitan ng kaparehong produkto na walang depekto, o ibalik agad ang bayad kasama ang monetary updating.

Ayon sa Labor Advisory No. 06, Series 2020, dapat ibigay ng employer ang final pay mo within 30 days pag umalis ka, pero puwede itong ma-extend kung may mas pabor na patakaran ang kumpanya (hal., collective bargaining agreement). Para naman sa Certificate of Employment, kailangan ibigay ito ng employer within three days mula sa petsa na hiningi mo ito, walang exception para dito.

If an online purchase arrives with a different model, the consumer may treat it as a defect, malfunction, or loss that is not the consumer’s fault. The consumer can then seek repair, replacement, or a refund. When the consumer opts for replacement or refund, the online merchant must receive the original goods back at no cost to the consumer, within a reasonable period unless the parties agree otherwise. If a refund has already been paid but the consumer cannot return the item because of the consumer’s fault, the consumer must immediately return the refund amount, subject to a proportionate price reduction.

Sa probasyon, kailangan ng employer na sabihin agad sa empleyado kung ano ang standards para maging regular. Ibig sabihin, sa mismong araw ng pag‑hire, dapat i‑brief ang empleyado kung anong performance o qualification criteria ang susukatin. Hindi puwedeng hintayin pa ang unang araw ng trabaho o mag‑set ng extra grace period; ang standards dapat klaro at ibinigay bago magsimula ang probasyon.

Para mag‑claim ng warranty, kailangan mong dalhin ang produkto kasama ang warranty card o resibo sa mismong nag‑benta (immediate seller). Kung retailer lang ang nag‑benta, obligasyon niya na ipasa ang claim sa distributor nang walang bayad sa iyo. Ang retailer ay subsidiarily liable kung parehong manufacturer at distributor ay hindi tumugon, pero hindi siya dapat mag‑honor ng warranty directly; ang kanyang tungkulin ay i‑forward ang claim sa distributor.

all_checks.text: Sa ilalim ng Omnibus Rules, ang sahod ay dapat bayaran sa legal tender (pera) at bawal gamitin ang vouchers, coupons, o anumang token kahit na hilingin ng empleyado. Kaya kung gusto ng may-ari na ibigay ang kalahati ng sweldo mo sa grocery coupons, hindi ito pinapayagan ng batas; kailangan bayaran kayo ng cash o ibang legal na pera.

Wages must be paid at least once every two weeks, or twice a month, so the interval between paydays cannot be longer than sixteen days, unless a force‑majeure event or something beyond the employer’s control stops payment, in which case the employer must pay as soon as the event ends.

Sa simpleng salita, ang employer dapat magbayad ng sahod hindi bababa sa isang beses kada dalawang linggo o dalawang beses sa isang buwan, at ang pagitan ng mga payday hindi dapat lumagpas ng 16 na araw. Kung may force majeure o ibang pangyayari na wala sa kontrol ng employer, pwede siyang mag‑delay pero kailangang bayaran agad pag natapos na ang sitwasyon. Kaya kung wala pang bayad ang kliyente pero wala namang ganitong dahilan, dapat pa rin kayong makatanggap ng sahod sa loob ng 16 araw mula noong huling payday.

A wage deduction for missing cash is only allowed if the employer is in a business where such deductions are a recognized practice and the employee is clearly shown to be responsible, is given a reasonable chance to explain why the deduction should not be made, the amount is fair, does not exceed the actual loss, and is not more than 20 % of the employee’s weekly wages. Moreover, it cannot be a withholding without the worker’s consent (Art 116) nor a deduction made merely to benefit the employer or secure continued employment (Art 117).

Ayon sa Section 6 ng Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code, kailangang mag‑payroll ang employer at ilahad nang hiwalay para sa bawat empleyado ang (1) haba ng panahon na binabayaran, (2) rate ng sahod (per month, week, day o hour), (3) halaga para sa regular na trabaho, (4) halaga para sa overtime, (5) anumang bawas, at (6) ang netong binayad. Kaya dapat tingnan ang payroll sheet kung may nakasulat ang mga ito.

If the employee is required to attend a safety briefing before the attendance clock is started, that time is considered hours worked because the law says hours worked include all time an employee is required to be on duty or at a prescribed workplace. The fact that the clock has not yet been turned on does not change the requirement‑based test.

Sa ilalim ng Labor Code, ang oras na ginugugol mo habang hinihintay na ma‑restart ang makina ay counted bilang oras ng trabaho kung kailangan ka ng employer na manatili sa workplace o kung ang paghihintay ay bahagi ng iyong trabaho. Ang Art. 84 ng Labor Code nagsasabing kasama sa oras ng trabaho ang lahat ng oras na kinakailangan mong naroroon sa prescribed workplace, at ang Omnibus Rules (Section 5) nag‑clarify na ang waiting time ay working time kapag ito ay integral part ng trabaho o required ng employer.

Every employer must give employees at least one hour off for regular meals. However, a shorter meal break of not less than twenty minutes is allowed if the employer meets any of these conditions: the work is non‑manual or not physically strenuous; the establishment operates at least sixteen hours a day; there is an actual or impending emergency or urgent work on machinery to avoid serious loss; or the work is needed to prevent serious loss of perishable goods. When a shorter break is given under any of those cases, it is counted as compensable working time. Additionally, coffee or rest breaks lasting from five to twenty minutes are also considered compensable working time.

Ayon sa Omnibus Rules, dapat bigyan ng employer ang mga empleyado ng hindi bababa sa isang (1) oras na time‑off para sa regular na pagkain. Samantala, ang mga coffee break o short rest periods na tumatagal mula limang (5) hanggang dalawampung (20) minuto ay itinuturing na bahagi ng oras ng trabaho, kaya dapat bayaran bilang kompensableng oras. Hindi kailangan mag‑qualify ang workplace sa anumang exemption para sa ordinaryong isang oras na meal period, at ang short rest break ay laging kompensable.

The rule says an employee must receive a night‑shift differential of at least ten percent of the regular wage for each hour worked between ten o’clock in the evening and six o’clock in the morning. This applies to all employees except those specifically exempted, such as government workers, very small retail or service establishments, domestic helpers, managerial staff, and workers engaged purely on a task, contract, or commission basis without supervision.

The cited provision only sets how often wages must be paid (at least once every two weeks or twice a month, with a 16‑day maximum interval) and does not address overtime compensation; therefore it does not provide the rule on whether a monthly salary includes extra hours.

For any employee covered by the rule, work that goes beyond eight (8) hours in a regular workday triggers overtime pay, which must be the regular wage plus at least twenty‑five percent (25%) of that wage for the extra hours.

Sa ilalim ng Art. 88 ng Labor Code, sinasabi na ang undertime na ginawa mo sa isang araw ay hindi puwedeng i‑offset o ibawas gamit ang overtime na kinita mo sa ibang araw. Kahit binigyan ka ng permiso para mag‑leave sa ibang araw, obligasyon pa rin ng employer na bayaran ang karagdagang kompensasyon na itinakda ng batas.
The rule says every employer must give each employee at least a 24‑hour consecutive rest period after six consecutive normal work days. The rest must follow those six days without interruption.
The law requires that each employee receive a rest period of not less than 24 consecutive hours after working six consecutive normal days.

Sa ilalim ng Omnibus Rules, dapat igalang ng employer ang gustong araw ng pahinga ng empleyado kung ito ay base sa relihiyon, basta isusulat ito at ipapadala sa employer nang hindi bababa sa pitong (7) araw bago ang gustong petsa. Pero, kung ang pagpili ng empleyado ay tiyak na magdudulot ng malubhang pinsala o hadlang sa operasyon ng negosyo at wala nang ibang paraan para maayos ito, pwede ang employer na magtakda ng ibang araw ng pahinga para sa empleyado, pero hindi bababa sa dalawang (2) araw sa isang buwan.

Under Article 94(a) of the Labor Code, every worker must receive his regular daily wage on a regular holiday unless the employer is a retail or service establishment that regularly employs fewer than ten workers; if the repair shop has ten or more employees, the exemption does not apply and holiday pay is still due even if the shop is closed.

Para sa mga rank‑and‑file workers, ang 13th month pay ay katumbas ng isang‑twelfth (1/12) ng basic salary mo sa loob ng isang kalendaryong taon, at dapat bayaran ng employer bago o sa Disyembre 24 bawat taon. Ang basic salary ay kinabibilangan ng lahat ng sahod o kita mo para sa trabaho, pero hindi kasama ang cost‑of‑living allowance, profit‑sharing, at iba pang benepisyo na hindi itinuturing na regular na sahod.

Sa ilalim ng batas, ang 13th month pay ay isang‑twelfth (1/12) ng basic salary mo sa loob ng isang taon, at obligadong ibigay ng employer sa lahat ng rank‑and‑file employees hindi lalampas ng Disyembre 24. Ang basic salary ay sumasaklaw sa lahat ng sahod o kita mo, pero hindi kasama ang cost‑of‑living allowance, profit‑sharing, at iba pang hindi regular na benepisyo.

The excerpt defines 13th‑month pay as one‑twelfth (1/12) of an employee’s basic salary for the calendar year and says employers must pay rank‑and‑file workers by December 24. However, the quoted portion does not contain any rule on how to compute a proportionate amount when a worker leaves before year‑end, so it only gives the general definition and deadline, not a proration formula.

The same statutory quotation states that 13th‑month pay equals one‑twelfth of the basic salary earned in a calendar year and must be paid no later than December 24. The excerpt does not include any provision for calculating a partial (proportionate) payment for an employee who departs mid‑year, so it only provides the general rule, not a specific proration method.

The regular‑employment test says a job is regular when the employee is hired to do activities that are usually necessary or desirable in the employer’s ordinary business or trade, unless the work is for a specific project whose completion was set at hiring or is seasonal work that lasts only for the season. The project exception applies when the undertaking’s end‑date is known at the time of engagement, and the seasonal exception applies when the work is of a seasonal nature and the employment ends with that season.

Sa Art. 295 ng Labor Code, may exception sa regular‑employment rule: kung ang trabaho ay seasonal in nature at ang employment ay para lamang sa haba ng season, itinuturing itong seasonal exception. Ibig sabihin, ang kontrata ay valid lang habang tumatagal ang picking season at natatapos kapag natapos na ang season.

The rule requires that, at the moment the employee is engaged on probation, the employer must clearly communicate the reasonable performance standards the employee must meet to qualify as a regular employee.

Sa probasyon, hindi dapat lumagpas ng anim (6) na buwan mula sa unang araw ng trabaho, maliban kung ang trabaho ay sakop ng apprenticeship agreement na nagtatakda ng mas mahabang panahon. Kung hindi learnable o apprenticeable, ang limit ay 6 buwan. Dapat ding ipaalam ng employer sa simula pa lang kung ano ang mga pamantayan para maging regular employee; kung hindi matugunan ang mga ito, puwedeng tapusin ang probasyon para sa just cause o dahil hindi pumasa sa nasabing standards.
For a closure or cessation of business, the rules define it as the complete or partial shutdown of the employer’s operations or establishment.

When an employer intends to close or cease operations, it must give a written notice to the workers and the Ministry of Labor and Employment at least one (1) month before the intended date. If the termination is due to installation of labor‑saving devices or redundancy, the employee gets separation pay of at least one (1) month pay or one (1) month pay for each year of service, whichever is higher. If the termination is for retrenchment to prevent losses or for closure not caused by serious business losses or financial reverses, the separation pay is one (1) month pay or at least one‑half (½) month pay for each year of service, whichever is higher, with any fraction of at least six (6) months counted as a whole year.

Sa ilalim ng Art. 300 ng Labor Code, kung gusto mong mag‑resign nang walang just cause, kailangan mong mag‑submit ng sulat na nag‑notice sa employer nang hindi bababa sa isang (1) buwan bago ang huling araw mo (see q1‑q3). Kung hindi ka mag‑notice, pwede kang papanagutin ng employer para sa damages (q4‑q5). May mga “just causes” kung saan hindi na kailangan ng notice: (a) seryosong insulto sa iyong dangal, (b) inhuman o hindi matiwasay na pagtrato, (c) krimen o paglabag ng employer laban sa iyo o pamilya mo, o (d) iba pang katulad na sitwasyon (q6‑q13).

Sa ilalim ng Labor Advisory No. 06‑2020, kailangang ibigay ng employer ang Certificate of Employment (COE) sa loob ng tatlong (3) araw mula sa petsa ng kahilingan mo. Walang binanggit na “better policy” exception para sa COE, kaya kung sinabing aasikasuhin pa nila ito sa susunod na quarter, technically lumalabag ito sa itinakdang deadline.

Sa conciliation‑mediation conference, ang default ay dapat mag‑representa ang mismong partido; hindi hinihikayat ang mga abogado maliban kung sila mismo ang humihiling o employer, o kung may lehitimong kinatawan. Kapag kailangan ng abogado, agent, o attorney‑in‑fact na lumahok para sa isang partido, kailangan nilang mag‑presenta ng special power of attorney, board resolution, o secretary’s certificate na nagpapatunay ng kanilang awtoridad, at ito ay required lamang kung ang partido ay lumipat ng rehiyon o nasa labas ng bansa, menor de edad o hindi kayang mag‑representa dahil sa pisikal na kondisyon, o kung namatay na ang partido at ang tagapagmana o awtorisadong kinatawan ang lalabas.

To enforce the warranty you only need to bring the product together with either the warranty card or the official receipt; the seller cannot ask for any other document. If the shop is an ordinary retailer (not the manufacturer’s showroom or a distributor), it must forward your claim to the distributor on your behalf at no cost to you. The retailer is only subsidiarily liable if both the manufacturer and distributor refuse to honor the warranty.

Para ma‑enforce ang warranty, kailangan mo lang dalhin ang produkto at ang warranty card o resibo sa mismong nag‑benta (immediate seller). Kung retailer ang nag‑benta, obligasyon niya na ipasa ang claim sa distributor nang walang bayad sa consumer. Kapag parehong hindi tumugon ang manufacturer at distributor, subsidiarily liable ang retailer at dapat niyang sagutin ang gastos para maayos o mapalit ang produkto. May karapatan pa rin ang retailer na habulin ang distributor o manufacturer para sa bayad.

When a seller or manufacturer gives an express warranty, the law requires the warranty to be written in clear, easily understood language and to include: the identity of the warrantor; the identity of the party to whom the warranty is extended; a description of the products or parts covered; a statement of what the warrantor will do if a defect, malfunction or non‑conformity occurs and who will pay for it; a description of what the consumer must do to claim the warranty; and the period within which the warrantor must act after notice of the problem. Any warranty that omits these elements is considered null and void.

Para mag-claim ng warranty, kailangan mo lang dalhin ang produkto kasama ang warranty card o resibo sa mismong nagbenta (immediate seller). Walang ibang dokumento na hihingin. Kung ang seller ay manufacturer showroom o distributor, dapat agad nilang ayusin o palitan ang item. Kapag ordinaryong retailer ang nagbenta, obligasyon niya na ipasa ang claim sa distributor nang walang bayad sa buyer; siya lang ang magdadala ng gastos kung hindi pa ito tinupad ng distributor o manufacturer.

Because you bought the blender at the manufacturer’s showroom, the law treats that showroom as the immediate seller. Art. 68 says the warranty must be honored right away when the immediate seller is the manufacturer’s factory or showroom. An ordinary retailer, on the other hand, is only subsidiarily liable: it must cover the warranty costs only if both the manufacturer and the distributor fail to honor it, and it may still pursue them for payment.

Art. 68 requires you to present the product together with the warranty card or receipt to the immediate seller. If that seller is the manufacturer’s showroom, the warranty is honored immediately; if it is a distributor, the distributor must honor it. An ordinary retailer is not the one to repair or replace the item; its duty is simply to forward your claim to the distributor at no cost to you, and it becomes liable only if both the manufacturer and distributor fail to comply.

Sa ilalim ng RA 7394, Art. 100, ang supplier ng durable o nondurable na produkto ay responsable kung may depekto na nagiging hindi angkop o bumababa ang halaga ng produkto, pati na kung hindi tugma sa label o ad. Kapag hindi naayos ang depekto sa loob ng 30 araw, pwede kang pumili ng isa sa tatlong remedyo: palitan ng kaparehong produkto na maayos, ibalik ang binayad na may monetary updating, o bawasan ang presyo nang proporsyonal. Pwede ring pahabain o paikliin ang correction period basta hindi bababa sa 7 araw at hindi hihigit sa 180 araw.

Sa ilalim ng Art. 101 ng Consumer Act, kung ang net content ng produkto ay mas mababa kaysa sa nakasaad sa lalagyan, label o ad, ang supplier ay may pananagutan. Bilang consumer, pwede mong piliin ang isa sa mga sumusunod: (a) bayaran ang proportionate price ng natanggap mong tiles; (b) dagdagan ang timbang o sukat na kulang; (c) palitan ang pack ng kaparehong klase, tatak o modelo na walang kakulangan; o (d) ibalik agad ang buong bayad kasama ang monetary updating at posibleng damages. Ang supplier ay mananagot lalo na kung ang panukat na ginamit ay hindi naka‑calibrate ayon sa opisyal na pamantayan.

When a repair shop fixes a product, it must automatically use adequate, new, original parts—or parts that meet the manufacturer’s technical specifications—unless the consumer has given explicit permission to use other parts. So, installing a used replacement without the consumer’s consent would not meet the rule’s requirement.

Under the Consumer Act, a seller commits a deceptive act if it represents a product as new, original or unused when in fact it is deteriorated, altered, reconditioned, reclaimed or second‑hand. Such false representation, whether made before, during or after the sale, is prohibited as a deceptive sales practice.

Sa ilalim ng Consumer Act, kung sinabing may sponsorship, approval, o affiliation ang isang produkto pero wala talaga, itinuturing itong deceptive practice. Ibig sabihin, ang seller na nag-claim na certified ang kettle pero hindi maipakita ang basehan ay maaaring lumabag sa batas dahil nagbigay ng false representation tungkol sa approval. Hindi kailangan patunayan agad na peke ang claim; ang mismong maling representasyon ay sapat na para ituring itong deceptive.

Under the Consumer Act, a seller commits a deceptive act when it falsely represents that a consumer product has characteristics it does not actually possess. If a shop tells a buyer that a printer includes a feature that the model lacks, that representation triggers the prohibition on deceptive sales practices.

The law declares it deceptive for a seller to claim a product has performance or characteristics it does not have. When a retailer advertises a printer with a feature that the sold model does not contain, this false representation falls within the prohibited deceptive sales act.

The law makes it illegal for anyone to spread an advertisement that is false, deceptive or misleading. An ad is considered false, deceptive or misleading when it does not comply with the Consumer Act or when it misleads in a material way. In deciding this, authorities look at the claims made, any combination of those claims, and whether the ad fails to disclose important facts or consequences about the product under the advertised or usual conditions.

Sa advertising, kung nag‑compare ka ng presyo, dapat sundin ang ilang kondisyon: kung dati mong presyo ang ginamit, kailangan na ang item ay na‑sell sa dating presyo loob ng 90 araw bago ang ad, o di kaya’y in‑offer ito for sale ng hindi bababa sa 4 weeks sa loob ng 90 araw. Kung wala ito, dapat ilahad sa ad kung kailan (date, time o season) nangyari ang dating sale. Kung future price naman ang binanggit, dapat ito ay e‑effective sa petsa na sinabi sa ad o sa loob ng 90 araw, at dapat panatilihin ng seller ang bagong presyo ng hindi bababa sa 4 weeks pagkatapos ng effective date, maliban kung may “circumstances beyond the seller’s control.” Kung competitor’s price ang kinompara, dapat ang presyo ng competitor ay para sa parehong produkto o serbisyo, na na‑sell o na‑advertise sa loob ng 90 araw at dapat representatibo sa local market.

Sa ilalim ng Consumer Act, Art. 81, bawal magbenta ng produkto nang mas mataas sa presyo na nakalagay sa price tag o label na nakikita ng publiko. Kung may price tag, iyon ang dapat sundin; hindi puwedeng i‑claim na lumang tag lang ‘yan. Ang probisyon ay hindi nagbubukod kung may pagkakaiba sa shelf tag at sa cashier, kaya dapat ibenta ayon sa nakasaad sa tag.

Ayon din sa Art. 81 ng Consumer Act, ang anumang consumer product ay hindi maaaring ibenta sa halagang mas mataas kaysa sa nakasaad sa price tag o sa price list na inilagay sa pinakamalapit na punto kung hindi praktikal ilagay ang tag. Kaya kung sinasabi ng cashier na mas mataas ang presyo kaysa sa nakalagay, labag ito sa batas.

Under the Consumer Act (RA 7394), a product is considered defective when it fails to provide the safety that a consumer rightfully expects, based on how the product is presented, the hazards reasonably expected in its normal use, and the time it was placed on the market. The law holds manufacturers, producers, and importers liable for damages caused by such defects, regardless of fault, unless they can prove they never marketed the product, the product had no defect, or the consumer or a third party was solely at fault.

Kung may permanent marks ang damit mo after ng laundry service, ayon sa Art. 102 ng Consumer Act, liable ang service supplier sa quality imperfection na nag‑decrease ng value ng serbisyo. Bilang consumer, pwede mong piliin ang isa sa mga remedyo: (1) ipagawa ulit ang serbisyo nang walang dagdag na bayad; (2) ibalik agad ang halagang binayaran mo, kasama ang monetary updating at anumang loss o damage; (3) bawasan ang presyo nang proportionate. Pwede rin ipag‑outsource ang reperformance sa qualified third party, pero ang risk at gastos ay nasa supplier.

Kapag may quality imperfection ang service—halimbawa, hindi maayos ang pagkaka‑repair ng speaker—ang service supplier ay liable. Bilang consumer, pwede kang pumili ng isa sa tatlong remedyo: (1) ipagawa ulit ang service nang walang dagdag na bayad; (2) kunin agad ang kabuuang bayad na may monetary updating; o (3) humingi ng proportionate price reduction.

Sa repair service, ang supplier ay obligadong gumamit ng tamang, bagong o orihinal na piyesa (Art. 103) at dapat mag‑perform ng maayos na serbisyo. Kung hindi naayos ang speaker, may tatlong opsyon mula sa Art. 102: (1) iparepair ulit ng supplier o ng qualified third party nang walang dagdag na bayad; (2) ibalik agad ang halagang binayad na may monetary updating; o (3) bawasan ang presyo nang proportionate.

Under Art. 102 of the Consumer Act, a service supplier is liable when the service is imperfect—meaning it is inadequate for the purposes a consumer reasonably expects or does not match the advertised description. The consumer may choose one of these remedies: have the service performed again at no extra charge, receive an immediate refund of the amount paid (with monetary updating and any loss or damage), or get a proportionate reduction of the price. The repeat performance can be assigned to a duly qualified third party, but the supplier bears all risk and cost.

You can start a consumer complaint with the DTI by submitting a petition or a letter‑complaint about the faulty appliance. The department may then open an investigation, and it must keep a system for logging, investigating and responding to complaints to make redress as easy as possible. Once the investigation ends, the consumer arbitration officer must decide the case within fifteen days.

If the cabinet you received is the wrong size and the mistake is not your fault, the online consumer may demand repair, replacement, refund, or any other remedy that the Consumer Act (RA 7394) provides. When you opt for a replacement or a refund, the merchant can require you to send back the originally delivered cabinet at no cost to you, as long as you do so within a reasonable time unless you and the merchant have agreed on a different arrangement. If the refund has already been paid but you cannot return the cabinet because of your own fault, you must immediately repay the refund amount, possibly reduced proportionally to the price of the goods.

Before filing a case in court or with a government agency, the aggrieved party must first use the digital platform’s internal redress mechanism. That step is considered exhausted only when the platform has not resolved the complaint within seven calendar days from the date it was filed.

The law says the e‑retailer or online merchant is primarily liable for indemnifying the consumer for any breach arising from the internet transaction. The e‑marketplace or digital platform is only treated as liable in the same way as the merchant when a finding shows they are the same entity. Thus, liability rests with the merchant unless the platform is legally identified as the same party; the platform does not automatically bear responsibility for all purchase problems.

Sa ilalim ng Art. 100 ng Consumer Act, refund o kapalit ay pwede lang kapag may imperpeksiyon sa produkto—halimbawa, depektibo o hindi tugma sa label. Kung wala itong sira at nag‑change ka lang ng isip, hindi nasasakop ng batas ang awtomatikong refund. Ang consumer ay may opsyon na mag‑refund kung hindi maayos ang depekto sa loob ng 30 araw, pero wala itong trigger kung walang depekto.

Para sa retail purchase, ang Art. 100 ay nagsasabing refund ay available lang kung may imperpeksiyon sa produkto at hindi ito na‑ayos sa loob ng 30 araw. Walang depekto, walang awtomatikong refund; ang retailer ay may subsidiaryong obligasyon sa warranty kung ang manufacturer o distributor ay hindi tumupad, pero hindi ito para sa simpleng pagbabago ng kulay na gusto mo.

Under the Omnibus Rules, wages must be paid in legal tender; using vouchers, coupons or any token that pretends to be money is absolutely prohibited, even if the employee asks for it. So a private café cannot legally satisfy wage obligations by giving store‑only vouchers.

The Consumer Act says it is unlawful to sell a consumer product at a price higher than the price shown on its tag, label or publicly displayed price list. Therefore, a hardware shop that charges more for a toolbox at checkout than the price displayed on the shelf is violating the price‑ceiling rule.

Para ma‑enforce ang warranty, kailangan ng mamimili na dalhin ang produkto kasama ang warranty card o resibo sa mismong nag‑benta (immediate seller) at walang ibang dokumentong pwedeng hingin. Kung ang nag‑benta ay ordinaryong retailer, obligasyon niyang ipasa ang claim sa distributor nang walang bayad sa mamimili; siya lang ang magdadala ng gastos kung parehong distributor at manufacturer ay hindi tumugon. Ang retailer ay subsidiarily liable kung parehong hindi nag‑honor ang distributor at manufacturer.

Where a service supplier provides a service that is imperfect—meaning it is not fit for its intended purpose or does not match the advertised description—the supplier is liable. The consumer may choose one of three remedies: (1) have the service performed again at no extra cost; (2) receive an immediate refund of the amount paid, with monetary updating; or (3) obtain a proportionate reduction in price. The supplier may also have a qualified third party redo the service, but the risk and cost remain with the supplier.

Ayon sa No Shortchanging Act (RA 10909, Sec. 4), obligadong ibigay ng negosyo ang eksaktong sukli sa consumer nang hindi na kailangang hilingin pa ito. Bawal din mag‑shortchange kahit maliit lang ang halaga, at hindi puwedeng mag‑bigay ng sukli sa ibang anyo kaysa sa tunay na pera o hingin ang pahintulot ng consumer para hindi sumunod sa probisyon.

Under the Omnibus Rules, a worker may be dismissed only for a just or authorized cause and only after due process. Due process requires the employer to give the worker a written notice that specifies the acts or omissions that are the grounds for dismissal, and the worker must be allowed a reasonable period to answer those allegations. The employer must also afford the worker ample opportunity to be heard and to defend himself, with a representative if desired.

The Internet Transactions Act gives an online consumer the right to seek repair, replacement, refund or other remedies when the product delivered is defective, malfunctions, is lost without the consumer’s fault, or does not conform to the contract. If the consumer opts for replacement or refund, the online merchant may require the return of the original goods at no cost to the consumer, and the return must be made within a reasonable period unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Ayon sa Labor Advisory No. 06‑2020, dapat ibigay ng employer ang final pay ng empleyado loob ng 30 araw mula siya umalis, maliban kung may mas pabor na patakaran ang kumpanya. Ang Certificate of Employment naman ay kailangang ibigay sa loob ng tatlong (3) araw mula sa kahilingan ng empleyado.

Sa ilalim ng Art. 102 ng Consumer Act, kung hindi maayos ang repair service, may tatlong remedyo ang consumer: (1) ipagawa ulit ang serbisyo nang walang dagdag na bayad, (2) hingin ang agarang refund kasama ang monetary updating, o (3) humingi ng proportionate price reduction. Bukod pa rito, ang Art. 103 nagtatakda na ang repair service ay dapat gumamit ng tamang, bagong, at orihinal na piyesa o katumbas nito, maliban kung pinayagan ng consumer.

It is a deceptive sales practice for a seller to represent that a consumer product is new, original, or unused when in fact it is deteriorated, altered, reconditioned, reclaimed, or second‑hand, and such misrepresentation is prohibited under Article 50 of the Consumer Act.

Para sa 13th month pay, ang batas (PD 851) nagde‑define na ito ay katumbas ng isang‑twelfth (1/12) ng basic salary mo sa loob ng isang kalendaryong taon. Ang basic salary ay lahat ng sahod at benepisyo na binabayaran mo para sa trabaho, pero hindi kasama ang cost‑of‑living allowance, profit‑sharing, at iba pang allowance na hindi bahagi ng regular na sahod noong 1975. Sa Memorandum Order No. 28 (1986), sinabing lahat ng rank‑and‑file employees dapat makatanggap ng 13th month pay hindi lalampas ng Disyembre 24 bawat taon.

Sa ilalim ng Internet Transactions Act (RA 11967) at ng JAO 24‑03, kung may depekto, malfunction, o pagkawala ng produkto na hindi mo kasalanan, may karapatan kang humingi ng repair, replacement, o refund. Kapag pinili mo ang replacement o refund, ang online merchant ay may karapatang ibalik ang orihinal na item na ipinadala sa’yo nang walang bayad sa’yo, at dapat itong gawin sa loob ng makatwirang panahon maliban na lang kung may ibang napagkasunduan. Kung nabayaran na ang refund pero hindi mo maibalik ang item dahil sa iyong pagkakamali, kailangan mong ibalik ang perang natanggap, maaaring may proportionate reduction sa presyo.

For a covered employee, the employer must disclose, at the time of engagement, the specific standards that will determine whether the employee will qualify as regular. This requirement applies regardless of the nature of the work and must be communicated before the probationary period begins.

An express warranty must state the period within which the warrantor will act after a defect is reported. Any warranty that omits that period is void, because any stipulation contrary to the article is without legal effect.

The supplied source only covers consumer warranties, requiring the warranty to specify its enforceable period and rendering any omission void. No provision on probationary employment is present in these materials, so the employment question cannot be answered from the given sources.

Kung kulang ang dami ng tiles kumpara sa nakasaad sa label, may liability ang supplier para sa quantity imperfection (Art. 101). May karapatan ang consumer na pumili ng isa sa mga remedyo: bayaran ang proporsyonal na presyo, dagdagan ang nawawalang timbang o sukat, palitan ng kaparehong produkto na walang depekto, o ibalik agad ang bayad kasama ang monetary updating.

To enforce a warranty you only need to bring the product plus the warranty card or official receipt to the seller you bought it from; no other paperwork is required. If that seller is an ordinary retailer (not the distributor or manufacturer), the retailer must, at no cost to you, forward your warranty claim to the distributor. The retailer’s duty stops there unless both the manufacturer and the distributor refuse to honor the warranty; in that situation the retailer becomes subsidiarily liable for the costs needed to satisfy the warranty, while still retaining the right to seek reimbursement from the upstream parties.

Sa ilalim ng Omnibus Rules, ang oras na ginugol mo sa paghihintay para sa restart ng makina ay itinuturing na oras ng trabaho kung ang paghihintay ay bahagi ng iyong trabaho o kung kinakailangan ka ng employer na mag‑wait. Kung ang paghinto ay dahil sa isang interruption na wala kang kontrol, at kailangan mong manatili sa lugar para mabilis na makabalik sa trabaho, ito rin ay counted bilang working time. Kaya, dapat isama ng employer ang oras ng waiting sa iyong sahod.

Ayon sa Consumer Act (RA 7394, Art. 81), bawal mag‑sell ng produkto nang walang tamang price tag o label na nakikita ng publiko, at hindi puwedeng ibenta ang produkto sa halagang mas mataas kaysa nakasaad sa tag. Kung ang item ay napakaliit para lagyan ng tag, puwede naman ilagay ang price list sa pinakamalapit na display point. Kaya, ang grocery na nag‑charge ng mas mataas kaysa sa nakalagay ay lumalabag sa batas.

For private companies, wages must be paid at least once every two weeks—or twice a month—so that the interval between paydays does not exceed sixteen days, unless a force‑majeure event or circumstances beyond the employer’s control temporarily prevents payment; in such cases the employer must pay the wages immediately after the event or circumstance ends.

Ayon sa Labor Advisory No. 06, Series 2020, dapat ibigay ng employer ang final pay mo within 30 days pag umalis ka, pero puwede itong ma-extend kung may mas pabor na patakaran ang kumpanya (hal., collective bargaining agreement). Para naman sa Certificate of Employment, kailangan ibigay ito ng employer within three days mula sa petsa na hiningi mo ito, walang exception para dito.

For all employers, the law requires that each employee receive a rest period of at least twenty‑four (24) consecutive hours after working six consecutive normal work days. This is the minimum weekly rest day that must be provided.

Ayon sa Art. 94 ng Labor Code, dapat bayaran ng employer ang regular daily wage ng lahat ng manggagawa sa regular holiday, pero may exemption kung ang establisyemento ay retail o service at regular na may mas mababa sa sampung (10) empleyado; kung umabot o lumagpas sa sampu, wala ang exemption. Kaya kung ang retail store mo sa Vigan ay may sampung o higit pang empleyado, dapat bayaran ka ng regular na sahod sa holiday; kung mas mababa sa sampu, hindi ka sakop ng obligasyong ito.

Kapag may sira ang biniling desk fan at hindi ito maayos ng supplier sa loob ng 30 araw, may karapatan ka bilang consumer na pumili ng isa sa tatlong remedyo: palitan ng bagong fan na kapareho ng klase at nasa maayos na kondisyon, ibalik agad ang perang binayad kasama ang monetary updating, o bawasan ang presyo nang proporsyonal. Pwede mo rin agad gamitin ang alinman sa remedyo kung ang pag-aayos ay makakasira pa sa kalidad o halaga ng fan. Ang supplier ay joint liable sa anumang depekto na nagbabawas ng gamit o halaga ng produkto.

Under the Consumer Act, the laundry service is liable for a quality imperfection. The consumer can choose, at no extra charge, to have the service performed again, but this no‑cost reperformance is only available when applicable; otherwise the consumer may get an immediate refund with monetary updating or a proportionate price reduction. If the service is redone by a third party, the supplier bears the risk and cost.

If an online purchase arrives with a different model, the consumer may treat it as a defect, malfunction, or loss that is not the consumer’s fault. The consumer can then seek repair, replacement, or a refund. When the consumer opts for replacement or refund, the online merchant must receive the original goods back at no cost to the consumer, within a reasonable period unless the parties agree otherwise. If a refund has already been paid but the consumer cannot return the item because of the consumer’s fault, the consumer must immediately return the refund amount, subject to a proportionate price reduction.

When a repair shop provides a service, it is automatically required to use adequate, new, original replacement parts—or parts that meet the manufacturer’s technical specifications—unless the consumer has given explicit authorization to use other parts.

Wages must be paid at least once every two weeks or twice a month, with the interval between payments not exceeding sixteen days, unless a force‑majeure event or other circumstance beyond the employer’s control temporarily prevents it; in such cases the employer must pay immediately after the event ends.  Also, wages must be paid in legal tender and the employer cannot use tokens, vouchers or any other substitute.  These rules together prohibit a private employer in Tanauan from withholding ordinary wages.

Sa probasyon, kailangan ng employer na sabihin agad sa empleyado kung ano ang standards para maging regular. Ibig sabihin, sa mismong araw ng pag‑hire, dapat i‑brief ang empleyado kung anong performance o qualification criteria ang susukatin. Hindi puwedeng hintayin pa ang unang araw ng trabaho o mag‑set ng extra grace period; ang standards dapat klaro at ibinigay bago magsimula ang probasyon.

Para mag‑claim ng warranty, kailangan mong dalhin ang produkto kasama ang warranty card o resibo sa mismong nag‑benta (immediate seller). Kung retailer lang ang nag‑benta, obligasyon niya na ipasa ang claim sa distributor nang walang bayad sa iyo. Ang retailer ay subsidiarily liable kung parehong manufacturer at distributor ay hindi tumugon, pero hindi siya dapat mag‑honor ng warranty directly; ang kanyang tungkulin ay i‑forward ang claim sa distributor.
